subject: Follow-up: GDPR DPA & SCC module selection - Acme discovery recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: GDPR DPA & SCC module selection - Acme discovery recap

Hi Jenna / Tom -

Great to speak today - thanks for the time and for walking through Acme's GDPR and procurement expectations. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

Recap from call:
- Scope: Acme will be data controller for customer data; Redwood will operate as processor for hosted inference and metrics.
- Regulatory asks highlighted: GDPR DPA, SCC module selection (we discussed controller->processor options), SOC 2 evidence, and your internal vendor security questionnaire.

Attachments (for legal/security review):
- Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf - our standard DPA with processor terms (redlines welcome).
- SCC_selection_matrix.xlsx - quick mapping of recommended SCC modules and where Redwood maps to each clause.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm Acme's preferred SCC module (controller->processor): Module 2 is the typical fit for controller->processor transfers - if you prefer an alternate module, flag it and we'll map obligations.
2) Please confirm timeline for legal review of the DPA (typical turnaround 3-5 business days for initial redlines).
3) Send over your vendor security questionnaire link or upload to the secure portal we can use (we can also complete a CSV/Excel).
4) Rishi (cc) will follow up with SOC 2 artifacts and a contact on our security team if you need direct Q&A.

Would you be open to a 30-minute sync next week to walk legal/security through the DPA + SCC matrix live? I can join with Rishi and Lauren.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>, security@acme.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GDPR DPA & SCC module selection - Acme discovery recap

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- SOC 2: Can you confirm Redwood's current SOC 2 status and date of the latest report? We typically request the most recent Type II report.
- SCC modules: Acme is the controller; we expect processor commitments under the controller->processor module. Can you confirm which SCC module you recommend and whether you will sign with Module 2 or Module 3?
- DPA timeline: Our legal team will aim to return comments within 5 business days once we receive a final DPA (we ran a quick internal check and that timeline is fine).
- Vendor questionnaire: I'll attach the questionnaire to my next email - for now, who should I send it to on your security team? Also, do you have an intake link (SecureFrame/Jira/other) we can use?

If you can confirm SOC 2 and SCC module recommendation, we can kick off legal review today. Appreciate it.

Best,
Jenna Park
Security Program Manager - Acme Corp
jenna.park@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GDPR DPA & SCC module selection - Acme discovery recap

Hi Jenna -

Thanks - answers below inline to keep everything in one thread.

- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II; the most recent report period ended March 2026. Rishi is sending the SOC 2 cover letter and remediation summary in a follow-up email. If your legal/security needs an encrypted copy, we can share via our secure portal (link below).

- SCC module recommendation: For controller->processor transfers, we recommend EU SCC Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) as the standard fit. We can accept Module 2. If you prefer Module 3 for any reason, we can map and confirm but Module 2 is the usual match for the flow you described. The attached SCC_selection_matrix.xlsx maps modules to Redwood obligations and shows the fit for Module 2.

- DPA: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf is attached - it reflects our standard processor DPA with SCC option language. Typical turnaround for initial redlines we see is 3-5 business days; we are happy to prioritize. Please route any redlines back to me.

- Vendor questionnaire: Please send the questionnaire to security@redwood.com. Our security team triages vendor questionnaires and will either complete directly or request a short call for clarifications. If you prefer, we can also accept uploads via SecureFrame - here is our intake link: https://secure.redwood.com/vendor-intake (for file uploads).

Suggested schedule: if you can confirm Module 2 and drop your DPA redlines by Wednesday (2026-07-15), we can have legal + security review completed and return a final DPA by the end of next week. Also happy to set up a 30-minute sync this week - I have availability Tuesday/Thursday afternoon (US PT) or Wednesday morning (EU).

Attaching again: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, SCC_selection_matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: GDPR DPA & SCC module selection - Acme discovery recap

Jenna / Marissa -

Quick note from the security side:
- Confirming SOC 2 Type II (period ended 2026-03). I can circulate the SOC 2 cover letter and a redacted report if helpful - please let me know preferred delivery (encrypted email or secure portal).
- We agree with Marissa that Module 2 is the appropriate SCC for controller->processor transfers. We'll support the mapping and any clause-level comments.
- For the vendor questionnaire: sending it to security@redwood.com is perfect. If you'd like, we can also pre-populate answers for standard sections (data flows, retention, subprocessors) to speed review.

Next steps (proposal):
1) Jenna sends questionnaire + any initial DPA redlines by 2026-07-15.
2) Rishi + Lauren review and return comments via DocuSign/HubSpot (we'll prepare DocuSign once terms are agreed).
3) If legal needs an exec escalation, loop in_______ (we can provide a point of contact).

Happy to jump on a quick call to go through any technical security items.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
